$note: How a release is decided here: release-please reads the conventional commits since a line's last
tag, opens a pull request that bumps that line's version and writes its RELEASES.md, and cutting
the tag is what MERGING that pull request does. `release.yml` is what the tag then starts.
THE NARRATIVE CHANGELOG IS NOT TOUCHED. src_vs_code/CHANGELOG.md is the human record — 122
paragraphs of prose, one per release — and `changelog-names-the-release.mjs` REFUSES an mcp
release that is not written up in it. `changelog-path` sends every generated file to RELEASES.md
instead, so the two never meet. This is option A of
todo/PLAN_release_please_meets_a_narrative_changelog.md, and it is the only option that keeps a
guard whose whole purpose is to make sure a person wrote something.
$order: WHAT CHANGES FOR A RELEASER, and it is the part worth reading before the first one.
The mcp line is GUARDED: `changelog-names-the-release.mjs` refuses the release unless
src_vs_code/CHANGELOG.md names that exact version and changelog-baseline.json lists it. Under
release-please the version is decided by the release pull request, so the prose has to be written
BEFORE that pull request merges — add the `## Server <version> — <date>` section and the baseline
entry to the release pull request itself, then merge it.
That makes the release pull request a CHECKPOINT rather than a button, which is the right shape:
the alternative is cutting the tag first and having the guard refuse afterwards, which leaves a
tag that must not be moved and a release that cannot proceed.
The other three lines are unguarded today, so nothing stops them — but they are unguarded because
nobody has turned them on, not because they do not deserve it. A design that only works while
three guards are off is not settled; see the plan's step 5.
$decided: DRAFT plus FORCE-TAG-CREATION, and the second is not optional. The action's own schema: "GitHub
does not create a Git tag for draft releases until they are published… Setting this to `true`
ensures the tag is created immediately." Without it there is no tag, `release.yml` triggers on
`push: tags`, and nothing would ever run — a silent deadlock. Learned on dew_flow_creds_for_devs
on 2026-09-21, where `draft` alone first shipped three releases PUBLISHED AND EMPTY.
The draft suits this repository exactly as it stands: release.yml already creates a draft, or
REUSES one it finds, and refuses outright to upload into a published release. release-please
making that draft first is the case it was already written for.
SEPARATE PULL REQUESTS, one per line. Four products with four audiences release at four
cadences — extension 0.50.0 against bugs 0.2.0 — and a combined pull request would tie them
together. It also keeps the tags arriving one at a time.
RELEASE TYPES ARE NOT UNIFORM. The extension's package.json IS its version and release.yml
refuses a tag that disagrees with it, so `node` fits it exactly. mcp, server and bugs carry no
version in the tree — the build injects it from the tag with -p:Version — so `simple` with a
version.txt is what finally gives them one. That file is a RECORD, not a new input.
